title: Sweet singers Dan Grissom and Pha Terrell
summary: He defends sweet band singers and recalls accompanying Grissom in Seattle.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them

blocks.x: Freddie Guy? Yeah. You mentioned earlier people like Dan Grissom and Pha Terrell with Andy Kirk's band. Jazz Critics, people who write about Jazz, have never had much use for those kind of singers. Naturally, everybody loves the way Louis sings, and we accept all the musicians who were singing, like Trummy and so on. But the sweet singers like that have really gotten a bit of a raw deal from all the things that you read in the history books. Now, in talking to musicians, you very often find that they like their work.
Oh, they were my favorite singers! I think Dan Grissom and Pha Terrell, you couldn't top 'em.
And they had a lot to do also with the popularity of those bands, I think...
Sure, they did. Sure. I'd like to talk to a critic sometime and have him start putting one of them down. I'd put him down so fast it would snap his head off.

I'd say, "What are you talkin' about, man. I love that way that guy sang." Dan Grissom. I heard him, I played the piano for him in Seattle one night. He sang... [SINGS... DE/I love you...] -- "At Dawning." Whew! You could have heard a pin drop in that joint. It was an after-hours joint. When he got through with that, there was just utter silence. Finally, somebody says, "WSHEW!" You know?
